t.1.88.1: I, Vasumanas, son of Uśadaśva, ask you, O lord of men, whether there is a world for me in heaven, or one renowned in the mid-region, O great-souled one; for I consider you a knower of the field of that dharma.
t.1.88.3: Vasumanā said: Those worlds that are mine, I give them to you; do not fall into the abyss, let them indeed be yours. Buy them, O king, even for a blade of grass, if accepting a gift is truly faulty for you.
t.1.88.2: As vast as the mid-air, the earth and the directions, and all that the radiant sun warms with its heat, so many are the worlds established in heaven; they are not finite, and they await you.
t.1.88.4: I do not recall ever having made a false sale, wary of anything wrongly taken from a mere child. Nor would I do what has never been done before by others, for I seek to know what is truly good in this matter.
t.1.88.6: I, Śibi Auśīnara, ask you, dear sir: are there worlds for me too here, whether resting in the mid-air or in heaven? For I consider you one who knows the field of that dharma.
t.1.88.5: Take those worlds, O king, as given by me, if a purchase is not to your liking. I shall not go back to them, O lord of men; let all those worlds indeed be yours.
t.1.88.7: Neither by word nor even in your heart, wise lord of men, did you ever scorn those who came seeking from you. Therefore endless worlds stand ready in heaven; they are like lightning in form, resounding and vast.
t.1.88.9: Just as you, O god among men, are of power equal to Indra's, and your worlds too are endless, so I today take no delight in a world given by another; therefore, Śibi, I do not welcome your gift.
t.1.88.8: Take possession of those worlds given by me, O king, if a purchase is not agreeable to you; and having given them away, I shall not enter those worlds to which you go and where you dwell.
t.1.88.10: Aṣṭaka said: If you will not accept our worlds from each of us one by one, O king, then all of us, having given them to you, shall go to hell.
t.1.88.12: Aṣṭaka said: Whose are these five golden chariots that are seen, which, standing on high, shine forth blazing like tongues of fire?
t.1.88.11: What you, good men, gave out of truthfulness and kindness, you gave to one who is worthy; but I dare not do what has never been done by me before.
t.1.88.14: Mount the chariot, O king, and stride forth through the sky; we too shall follow after you when the time comes.
t.1.88.13: For these five golden chariots will carry you; standing on high, they shine forth, blazing like tongues of fire.
t.1.88.15: Now we must all go together, for we have won heaven. Here before us appears our spotless path to the abode of the gods.
t.1.88.16: Having mounted their chariots, all those best of kings set forth, striding across heaven with their radiance and enveloping heaven and earth with their dharma.
t.1.88.17: I thought that I alone would be the first to go, for the great-souled Indra is in every way my friend. Why then has this Śibi Auśīnara alone outstripped our horses with all his speed?
t.1.88.18: This son of Uśīnara gave, for the journey along the path of the gods, all the wealth he had acquired; therefore Śibi is indeed the best of us.
t.1.88.20: Then Aṣṭaka, out of curiosity, questioned once more his maternal grandfather, who was like Indra: "I ask you, O king, tell me the truth: from where are you, whose are you, and whose son are you? For what you have done, no other kṣatriya or brāhmaṇa in the world besides you could have done."
t.1.88.19: Generosity, austerity, truth and also righteousness, modesty, prosperity, forbearance and likewise endurance, O gentle one: these, O king, abide by his understanding in the matchless King Śibi, who is free from cruelty. Because he is of such conduct and restrained by modesty, therefore Śibi surpassed you with his chariot.
t.1.88.21: I am Yayāti, the son of Nahuṣa and the father of Pūru, and here I was a universal sovereign. I tell a secret matter to my own: I am openly your maternal grandfather.
t.1.88.23: I gave to the brāhmaṇas this entire earth, full of mounts, together with cows, gold and the choicest riches; there were a hundred arbudas of cows on that occasion.
t.1.88.22: He conquered this whole earth; and having tethered them on the sacrificial ground, I gave to the brāhmaṇas pure, single-hoofed, handsome horses fit for sacrifice. It is then that the gods become partakers of merit.
t.1.88.24: By my truth stand heaven and earth, and by it likewise fire blazes among men; never has a word of mine been spoken in vain, for the good revere truth. All the gods, the sages and the worlds are to be honored through truth: this is my settled conviction.
t.1.88.26: Thus that great-souled king, the vanquisher of enemies, was truly rescued by his own daughter's sons; leaving the earth, he of supremely noble deeds went to heaven, having pervaded the world with his deeds.
t.1.88.25: Whoever, free of envy, should relate the story of all of us who have won heaven just as it happened, as learned from the foremost of the twice-born, he would attain the same world as ours.
